title.en: Economic environment in India: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation
title.kn: ಭಾರತದ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಪರಿಸರ: ಉದಾರೀಕರಣ, ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಜಾಗತೀಕರಣ

hook.en: Before 1991 an Indian firm needed a licence to make more scooters, and families waited years to buy one. In 1991 India changed course with liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation.
hook.kn: 1991ಕ್ಕೆ ಮೊದಲು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸ್ಕೂಟರ್ ತಯಾರಿಸಲು ಪರವಾನಗಿ ಬೇಕಿತ್ತು; ಜನರು ವರ್ಷಗಟ್ಟಲೆ ಕಾಯುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು. 1991ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತ ಉದಾರೀಕರಣ, ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಜಾಗತೀಕರಣದ ದಾರಿ ಹಿಡಿಯಿತು.

objectives.en: State the impact of LPG on business

narration.en: Before 1991 an Indian firm needed a licence to make more scooters, and families waited years to buy one. In 1991 India changed course with liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation.
narration.kn: 1991ಕ್ಕೆ ಮೊದಲು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸ್ಕೂಟರ್ ತಯಾರಿಸಲು ಪರವಾನಗಿ ಬೇಕಿತ್ತು; ಜನರು ವರ್ಷಗಟ್ಟಲೆ ಕಾಯುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು. 1991ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತ ಉದಾರೀಕರಣ, ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಜಾಗತೀಕರಣದ ದಾರಿ ಹಿಡಿಯಿತು.

body.en: Liberalisation freed industry from unnecessary controls: licensing was abolished in most industries, and firms got freedom in deciding scale, prices and imports. Privatisation gave the private sector a greater role, including disinvestment in public sector units. Globalisation integrated India with the world economy through freer trade and foreign investment.

points.en: Liberalisation: end of licence raj in most industries

narration.kn: ಉದಾರೀಕರಣ ಅನಗತ್ಯ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ತೆಗೆಯಿತು; ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ ಖಾಸಗಿ ವಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪಾತ್ರ ನೀಡಿತು; ಜಾಗತೀಕರಣ ಭಾರತವನ್ನು ವಿಶ್ವ ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಬೆಸೆಯಿತು.

title.en: On the board: LPG at a glance

narration.en: Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

say.en: In 1991, the New Economic Policy rested on three pillars.
Liberalisation: remove unnecessary controls and licences.
Privatisation: a bigger role for private firms, and disinvestment in PSUs.
Globalisation: link India with the world through trade and investment.
Under each pillar, note one key action.
The impact: more competition, demanding customers, fast technology change, and the need for market orientation.

narration.en: Sort each reform since 1991 into liberalisation, privatisation or globalisation.

explanation.en: Liberalisation removed controls, privatisation widened the private sector's role, and globalisation linked India with the world economy.

text.en: Industrial licensing abolished for most industries
Firms free to decide their scale of business
Government sells part of its shares in PSUs
Fewer industries reserved for the public sector
A state-owned airline is sold to a private group
Lower import duties and freer trade
Foreign direct investment allowed in more sectors

body.en: After 1991, competition increased, customers became more demanding, technology changed rapidly, firms needed to change, human resources had to be developed, firms shifted to market orientation, and public sector units lost budgetary support.

points.en: Loss of budgetary support to public sector

narration.kn: ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿತು, ಗ್ರಾಹಕರು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಬೇಡಿಕೆಯುಳ್ಳವರಾದರು, ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಬದಲಾಯಿತು, ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ದೃಷ್ಟಿ ಅಗತ್ಯವಾಯಿತು.

problem.en: An old Bengaluru television maker had a 10-year waiting list before 1991. After 1991, foreign brands entered, prices fell, and customers began demanding flat screens and after-sales service. Identify three impacts of LPG seen here.

steps.en: Customers demanding new features and service: more demanding customers.
The shift to flat screens: rapidly changing technological environment.

answer.en: Increasing competition, more demanding customers, and rapid technological change.

narration.en: Recap. NEP 1991 introduced liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation. Licensing was abolished in most industries. Competition and customer expectations increased sharply.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. 1991ರ ಹೊಸ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ನೀತಿ ಉದಾರೀಕರಣ, ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ, ಜಾಗತೀಕರಣ ತಂದಿತು. ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪರವಾನಗಿ ರದ್ದಾಯಿತು. ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ ಮತ್ತು ಗ್ರಾಹಕರ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷೆ ತೀವ್ರವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದವು.
